name: revisit-horizon
question: How long can the camera look away before the generated world is no longer found again on return, and does archived-view memory extend that horizon?
hardware: Lambda gpu_1x_h100_pcie (both arms on the same GPU model)

scene_selection.rule: GC split, sort by sha256('revisit-horizon-2026-11-15:' + task_id), first 20 after excluding development scenes

path.actions: WAIT, RIGHT x3, WAIT x H, LEFT x3, WAIT (one action = one 1-second chunk; native fixed controls)
path.turn_note: 3 chunks at 68 deg/s commanded; realized rotation was measured at about 0.9 of commanded on GC007/GC001, i.e. about 180 degrees. Decided on those two development scenes only.

stock.note: rolling window 18 latent frames incl. 6 sink frames (about 4.5 s)

memory.note: exact bounded pose memory: 24-frame archive, pose-redundancy eviction, 10 retrieved frames, native RoPE, same attended budget. Valid at every horizon here because the frames added during the stationary hold are pose duplicates and are evicted first; the outbound sweep and start frames stay archived. Chosen on GC007/GC001 before this run.

arms.memory_v2_disk: not included: it had not passed its fixed-path step 1 when this file was frozen

judge.primary: released PlayWorld verifier (gate + rubric + released aggregation) through worldsync.gemini_vertex_judge, Vertex gemini-3.1-pro-preview
judge.task_record: each scene's released GC record (image, caption, policies, its own rubric questions) with `prompt`, `action_sequence`, `action_sequence_steps` and `action` replaced by the scripted objective below

objective_template.0: Turn right 180 degrees, then turn back to the original view.
objective_template.6: Turn right 180 degrees, wait for 6 seconds, then turn back to the original view.
objective_template.12: Turn right 180 degrees, wait for 12 seconds, then turn back to the original view.
objective_template.24: Turn right 180 degrees, wait for 24 seconds, then turn back to the original view.

judge.score_per_video: mean of the calls' official scores
judge.world_model_name_shown_to_judge: LingBot-World-Infinity (same for both arms; no arm label)

metrics.primary: judged official score (1-5), mean of 2 calls
secondary: DINOv2-small CLS cosine, final frame vs frame 12 (end of the opening hold) and vs frame 0
judge field revisit_observed (yes counts per arm)

analysis.paired: memory minus stock per horizon over scenes with both arms complete; bootstrap 95% CI over scenes (10000 draws, seed 11); wins/ties/losses
analysis.curve: mean score and mean DINO vs horizon for both arms with bootstrap CIs (PNG)
analysis.pooled: paired difference pooled over horizons 6, 12, 24 with scenes as the resampling unit
analysis.truncation_rule: generation order is horizon 12, 24, 6, 0, scenes in hash order, stock then memory. If the run is cut at the 12:00 PST Lambda hard stop, each horizon is reported on the scenes whose two arms both completed, with the count stated; no horizon is dropped silently.
analysis.examples: strips for 4 scenes chosen by rule at horizon 12: the two largest and the two smallest paired judged differences (ties broken by hash order)

prediction_on_record: On development scenes memory lifted DINO at H=6 from about 0.3-0.4 to about 0.78. We expect a positive paired DINO difference at H>=6 and little difference at H=0 (the start view is still inside the stock window). Whether the judged score moves is unknown.
limits: scripted actions and objective, not the PlayWorld agent player: not a leaderboard score
rotation-only path; the audit found forward-then-back returns are not helped
Gemini preview model on Vertex; within-video judge SD was about 0.35 in earlier runs
